subtype: Stage 1: The juicy piece of news [Actor]
passage:
Dear Diary,
Today at break I went to the office to give Ma'am my permission slip. Swati from my class was sitting on the bench outside, crying into her dupatta. Then I heard the office lady say on the phone, "...her father, the hospital, the whole family is..." and then she shut the door.
I walked back to class so fast. My heart was going thump thump. Nobody else knows! Not even Meenu, and Meenu knows everything. I felt like the most important girl in class 4. I kept thinking of how everyone would look at me if I told them.
I feel a bit bad for Swati. She looked really sad. But I also want to tell someone SO much.
Neelam

qa.q: Where was Swati sitting when Neelam saw her?
qa.a: Swati was sitting on the bench outside the office, crying into her dupatta.

qa.q: Why is Neelam so excited about what she heard?
qa.a: She knows something no one else does, not even Meenu, and she likes imagining how everyone would look at her if she told.

qa.q: What could Neelam do at this moment instead of passing it on?
qa.a: She could keep the half-heard words to herself, since she did not hear the whole story, and maybe just be kind to Swati tomorrow.

qa.q: How might Swati feel if the story spreads around class?
qa.a: She would likely feel hurt and embarrassed, because her family trouble is private and she is already upset. 😢

grounding: It shows a child who sees a crying classmate and overhears a fragment about her family, feeling important and eager to share it.

passage: The school in Rampura had only four classrooms and one tin-roofed office. At lunch Preeti went to fill her bottle at the hand pump near the office and saw Jyoti on the step, wiping her eyes with both wrists. Inside, the headmaster was talking to Jyoti's uncle. Preeti caught only "...land... her father... in the city now..." before Jagdish-ji the peon shooed her away. She ran back to the neem tree where the girls were eating. Her cheeks were hot. Words bubbled in her mouth like a boiling pot. She sat down, opened her tiffin, and leaned toward the others. "Guess what I just heard," she began, feeling taller than she had all week.

qa.q: What did Preeti go to fill near the office?
qa.a: She went to fill her bottle at the hand pump.

qa.q: What was Preeti feeling as she sat down under the neem tree?
qa.a: She felt excited and important, bursting to share the words she had heard, like she was taller than all week.

qa.q: What turning point is available to Preeti right now?
qa.a: She could stop before she says more, remember she only heard a few words, and choose not to share Jyoti's private news.

qa.q: How might Jyoti experience it if the girls start talking?
qa.a: She would likely feel exposed and more upset, since she was already crying about something private.

grounding: It illustrates a child who sees a classmate crying and catches a piece of her family news, feeling important and eager to tell.

subtype: Stage 1: The juicy piece of news [Actor]
passage:
Class teacher's note, Monday

At recess Ayesha hurried back from the office corridor, eyes bright, and pulled two classmates into a corner. I heard her say, "I know something about Tanya. Something big."

Earlier, Tanya had been crying outside the principal's office with her mother. Ayesha, passing by, had heard a few words about "moving" and "her father."

Ayesha looked thrilled, almost puffed up.

I called her over and asked gently what she had seen. She told me, then added, "But I only heard a little bit." I said that a little bit can hurt a lot if it is passed on, and that Tanya was having a sad day.

Ayesha's face fell. She said she wouldn't tell. I will check on Tanya after lunch.

— Pradeep Sir

qa.q: Where had Tanya been crying?
qa.a: Outside the principal's office.

qa.q: How did Ayesha feel when she knew something the others didn't?
qa.a: She felt excited and important, almost puffed up, eager to share it.

qa.q: What did Pradeep Sir do well?
qa.a: He stopped Ayesha gently before she spread it, helped her see a fragment can hurt a lot, and planned to check on Tanya.

qa.q: How might Tanya feel if the fragment had spread?
qa.a: She would likely feel hurt and embarrassed on an already sad day, with classmates whispering about her family.

grounding: A teacher's note shows Ayesha, having overheard a fragment about a crying classmate's family, feeling important and eager to tell.

subtype: Stage 1: The juicy piece of news [Actor]
passage:
Wednesday

Today I saw Neelam crying outside the office with her mummy. I heard the principal say "sorry about your grandfather" and "take as many days as you need."

Nobody else saw. Only me!

In class everyone was asking where Neelam went. I almost told them. I had the words right in my mouth. It felt like holding a hot samosa, like I would burst if I didn't tell.

I didn't tell them. Yet.

But I kept thinking how Riddhi and Mahi would look at me if I knew something they didn't. Like I was important.

Now I am in bed and I feel a bit funny about it. Neelam was crying. Maybe it's not a nice thing to tell.

— Maria

qa.q: What did the principal say to Neelam's mummy?
qa.a: "Sorry about your grandfather" and "take as many days as you need."

qa.q: Why did Maria almost tell the class?
qa.a: Maria felt excited and important to know something no one else did, and imagined how Riddhi and Mahi would look at Maria.

qa.q: What would you advise Maria to do tomorrow?
qa.a: Keep it private and perhaps be kind to Neelam when Neelam comes back, since it is Neelam's sad news, not a story to share.

qa.q: How might Neelam feel if the class already knew when she came back?
qa.a: She would probably feel upset and exposed, having her private sadness spread without her say.

grounding: Maria's diary shows her overhearing a fragment about a crying classmate's family and feeling important and eager to tell it.

subtype: Stage 1: The juicy piece of news [Actor]
passage:
Shalini was sent to fetch chalk from the headmaster's room at the village school near Hassan. At the door she stopped.

Gauri from her class was inside, crying, while her father spoke quietly with the headmaster. Shalini heard "the loan" and "the land" and "we may have to leave."

She ran back with the chalk, her heart pounding. She knew something! Something nobody else knew!

At the water tap during break, her classmate Karthik was filling his bottle. Shalini tugged his sleeve. "Guess what I know about Gauri."

Karthik looked up, curious. "What?"

Shalini opened her mouth. Then she remembered Gauri's red eyes, the way her shoulders shook.

"Tell me!" Karthik said.

Shalini hesitated, the secret still warm and exciting in her chest, and not sure anymore whether it was hers to give.

qa.q: What was Shalini sent to fetch?
qa.a: Chalk from the headmaster's room.

qa.q: What was Shalini feeling as she ran back with the chalk?
qa.a: She was excited and felt important, her heart pounding because she knew something nobody else did.

qa.q: What could Shalini do at the water tap?
qa.a: Tell Karthik it isn't hers to share, because Gauri was upset and the news is Gauri's family's private business.

qa.q: How might Gauri feel if the class found out?
qa.a: She would probably feel ashamed and hurt, on top of worrying about leaving.

grounding: Shalini overhears a fragment about a crying classmate's family and feels important and eager to tell, hesitating on the edge of sharing it.

On Tuesday, Elif was sent to the school office in Copenhagen with the class register. Outside the door sat Freja from her class, crying into her sleeve. Through the half-open door Elif heard the secretary say, "...her father has moved out, so her mother will collect her from now on..."
Elif walked back slowly, her heart thumping. Nobody else knew. Just her. She felt taller somehow, as if she were carrying something heavy and shiny.
At the coat hooks, Lars asked, "What took you so long?"
Elif's mouth opened. The words were right there, bursting to get out. "I know something," she whispered, eyes wide. "Something big about Freja."

qa.q: Who was crying outside the school office?
qa.a: Freja from Elif's class was crying into her sleeve outside the door.

qa.q: How did Elif feel as she walked back knowing something nobody else knew?
qa.a: She felt important and excited, as if she were carrying something heavy and shiny, and she was eager to tell.

qa.q: What could Elif do at the coat hooks instead of telling Lars?
qa.a: She could keep what she overheard to herself, or quietly ask a teacher whether Freja is okay, because it is Freja's private family business.

qa.q: If you were Freja, what would you want Elif to do with what she heard?
qa.a: Freja would probably want it kept private, and maybe a kind word, not whispers at the coat hooks.

grounding: Shows a child who overhears a fragment about a crying classmate's family and feels important and eager to tell.
